features.note: Direct, relay, server authority and observer convergence are automated in M0; late join, reconnect and persistence remain for M1.

Typed move, look and setCrouch enter through ComponentInput and the production PlayerBodyUpdatePacket path. Direct and Relay validate ownership rejection, server/observer convergence for body quaternion plus head look angles, a third late joiner, stable actor identity on reconnect, deterministic latency/jitter/duplication/reordering, strict five-action replay, persistent position/rotation, and transient look/crouch reset across reconnect and save/reload.

Typed use, place and dig run through the production input/miner path with Direct and Relay authority/observer convergence, event correlation, server-origin rejection, unreachable-target rejection, a third late-joining client, actor reconnect, deterministic latency/jitter/duplication/reordering, and server save/reload persistence.

features.productionEntry: TerrainUpdater.SetUpdateLocation -> TerrainViewDistancePacket -> TerrainSyncChunkListPacket / revisioned terrain change packets
features.note: A deterministic one-server/three-client Direct and Relay scenario proves unloaded versus loaded cells, real ComponentInput movement across TerrainUpdater's eight-block hysteresis, authoritative chunk delivery, monotonic per-chunk revisions under a stale full snapshot plus 100% duplication and 50% reordering, observer and late-join baselines, stable-identity reconnect, strict two-action replay, and persisted terrain with in-memory revision reset after world reload.

A deterministic one-server/three-client Direct and Relay scenario creates a real Cow, applies a production ComponentBody impulse, and proves authoritative body convergence. It then reuses an entity ID across remove/add generations and injects stale loads under 100% duplication and 50% reordering, proving replacement and tombstone convergence, late join, stable-identity reconnect, save/reload persistence, strict two-action replay, and client rejection of server-only lifecycle controls.

features.productionEntry: ComponentInput / ComponentInventoryBase -> MoveItemPacket / ActiveSlotChangePacket / PlayerDropPacket -> revisioned InventorySyncPacket
features.note: A one-server/three-client Direct and Relay scenario drives real move, active-slot and drop production paths. It proves session ownership against a forged observer packet, request-ID idempotency under 100% duplication, monotonic inventory revisions under stale reordering, observer and late-join convergence, stable-identity reconnect, chest persistence, and strict replay.

The same deterministic scenario uses the real melee ray and server-authoritative reach check, proves forged hit geometry and observer respawn impersonation cannot mutate state, synchronizes health/damage with entity lifecycle and monotonic revisions, rejects stale rollback, kills and respawns the actor exactly once under duplicated packets, and verifies observer, late join, reconnect, save/reload and strict seven-action replay.

A deterministic one-server/three-client Direct and Relay scenario drives production time, precipitation, fog and lightning requests. It proves rejection outside creative mode, same-revision authoritative healing of optimistic client time/weather state, Playing-session authority, rejection of forged authoritative state, monotonic weather revisions under stale packets plus 100% duplication and 50% reordering, observer convergence, current-state baselines for late join and stable-identity reconnect, save/reload persistence, and strict eight-action replay. Lightning is verified as a live event and is intentionally not replayed as historical state to late joiners.

The same Direct and Relay scenario sends production sleep and wake requests, rejects cross-player sleep impersonation and forged client fire state, synchronizes explicit ignition and extinguish state with lifecycle-aware monotonic revisions, verifies stale-packet rejection under deterministic duplication/reordering, and covers observer, late join, reconnect, save/reload and strict replay boundaries.

features.productionEntry: ComponentGui / ComponentRider -> ComponentMountPacket -> lifecycle-bound authoritative rider/mount relation
features.note: A deterministic one-server/three-client Direct and Relay scenario uses real Boat entities and the production rider path. It rejects cross-player rider impersonation, forged authoritative state, stale expected revisions, invalid lifecycle generations, occupied targets and out-of-range requests; proves both rider and mount projections converge under 100% duplication and 50% reordering; reuses a mount entity ID across generations and records explicit lifecycle rejection metrics; verifies observer, late join, rider removal, stable-identity reconnect, safe-dismount save/reload semantics, and strict seven-action replay.

features.productionEntry: SubsystemElectricity / editable logic packets / PlayerInteractPacket / SubsystemMovingBlocks
features.note: A deterministic one-server/three-client Direct and Relay scenario drives authoritative edits for adjustable delay gates, batteries, buttons, switches, pistons, memory banks, truth tables, signs and dispensers, plus real switch interaction, electricity revisions and moving-block/piston lifecycles. It rejects server-only controls, cross-player impersonation, out-of-range requests, forged state and stale expected revisions; proves request-ID idempotency, monotonic revisions, generations and tombstones under 100% duplication and 50% reordering; keeps same-ID untagged moving sets distinct through wire-stable instance IDs; reconciles preloaded moving sets and replays a hard-bounded deferred editable baseline after terrain streaming; and verifies observer, late join, stable-identity reconnect, save/reload persistence and strict seventeen-action replay.
